Run Cucumber tests in a testthat context

Source: R/test.R
run.Rd

Call run() in a tests/testthat/test-*.R file to run the feature files alongside the package's testthat tests.

Usage

run(
  path = ".",
  filter = NULL,
  tags = NULL,
  reporter = if (is.null(testthat::get_reporter())) CucumberProgressReporter$new(),
  strict = TRUE,
  dry_run = FALSE,
  name = NULL,
  features = NULL,
  fail_fast = FALSE,
  retry = 0,
  order = "defined",
  ...
)

Arguments

path

Path to the directory containing the .feature files. Its subdirectories are searched too. If run() is placed in a tests/testthat/test-*.R file and you call testthat::test_dir or similar, it runs in the tests/testthat directory. The default value "." finds all feature files in the tests/testthat directory.

filter

If not NULL, run only the feature files whose name matches this regular expression.

tags

If not NULL, run only the scenarios that match this tag expression, e.g. "@smoke and not @slow".

reporter

A CucumberReporter, or NULL to report nothing of its own. In a testthat run, it defaults to NULL, leaving the output to testthat's reporter, which reports each scenario as a test. Outside of one, like in the console, it defaults to CucumberProgressReporter, as there is no testthat reporter to show the run.

strict

If FALSE, pending and undefined steps don't fail the run.

dry_run

If TRUE, match steps to step definitions without running steps or hooks.

name

If not NULL, run only the scenarios whose name matches any of these regular expressions.

features

If not NULL, run only these feature files, relative to path. A directory runs the feature files in it and its subdirectories. Add :line to run only the scenario at that line, e.g. "addition.feature:12". An empty vector runs no scenario. Empty strings, like the empty lines of a rerun file, are ignored.

fail_fast

If TRUE, skip the scenarios after the first failed scenario.

retry

How many times to run a failed scenario again, until it passes. Only failed scenarios are retried, not pending, undefined or ambiguous ones.

order

The order to run scenarios in: "defined", the order of the feature files and of the scenarios in them, "reverse", or "random". "random:<seed>", like "random:1234", runs them in the random order of that seed. Without a seed, the seed is chosen and shown, to run them in the same order again.

...

Additional arguments passed to grepl().

Value

NULL, invisibly.

Details

Each run() is a run of its own: its before_all() and after_all() hooks run once for each run(), so twice if two test files call run(). Step definitions, hooks and parameter types are kept until testthat's run ends, as testthat runs the setup-*.R files that define them once for all test files. Outside of a testthat run, like when run() is called in the console, they're kept until run() returns, and code deferred to testthat::teardown_env() runs when it returns. run() then attaches testthat for the steps' expectations, runs every scenario, reports them with CucumberProgressReporter and fails with "Test failures." if one of them failed.

run() in a parallel testthat run, with Config/testthat/parallel: true, is an error: testthat would delete the snapshot files of its feature files as unused.

testthat runs the setup-*.R files before run(), so for them to define steps without cucumber::, call library(cucumber) in tests/testthat.R.

Skip scenarios in a before_all() or before() hook, not with skip() before run() in its test file: testthat deletes the snapshot files of feature files that a run of every test file didn't run.

To get the results of a run, use test(), which returns them like testthat::test_dir().

Behavior






Feature: Running scenarios alongside testthat tests


run() in a tests/testthat/test-*.R file runs the feature files in tests/testthat
as part of the package's testthat tests, e.g. with testthat::test_local() or devtools::test().
It chooses what to run like test(), with filter, features, tags and name.
testthat's reporter reports each scenario as a test of the test file that calls run(), and a
failed step by its text and a warning, at its line of the feature file.
Pass a reporter to run() to report the run with cucumber's reporter too.


run() isn't supported in a parallel testthat run, with Config/testthat/parallel: true: it's an error.


run() can also run feature files outside of a testthat run, like in the console. It then attaches
testthat for the steps' expectations, runs every scenario and fails if one of them failed.
Its step definitions and hooks are cleared when it returns.

    Then the result is 2

    •

    testthat::test_local()
    • 

  • Then it passes

  • And it ran "Scenario: Adding one"
    • 

  • And it ran "calculate adds one"
    •

Scenario: Each scenario is a test of the test file that calls run()
  • Given a file named "tests/testthat/setup-steps.R" with
    given("I calculate", function(context) {
  context$result <- calculate(1)
})
then("the result is {int}", function(n, context) {
  expect_equal(context$result, n)
})
    •

    testthat::test_local(reporter = "silent")
    •

Scenario: testthat's reporter shows the line of the feature file where the step failed
  • Given a file named "tests/testthat/setup-steps.R" with
    given("I calculate", function(context) {
  context$result <- calculate(1)
})
then("the result is {int}", function(n, context) {
  expect_equal(context$result, 3)
})

Scenario: run() outside of a testthat run runs every scenario, and fails if one failed


Steps can use testthat's expectations, as run() attaches testthat.
  • Given a file named "features/calculate.feature" with

    Feature: Calculate
  Scenario: Adding one
    Then one plus 1 is 2

  Scenario: Adding two
    Then one plus 2 is 4

  Scenario: Adding three
    Then one plus 3 is 4
    • 

  • And a file named "features/steps.R" with
    then("one plus {int} is {int}", function(n, sum, context) {
  expect_equal(1 + n, sum)
})
    • 

  • When I run outside of a testthat run and it fails
    source("features/steps.R")
run("features")
    • 

  • Then it fails with
    Error:
! Test failures.
    • 

  • And the scenarios have these results:
    scenariostatus
    Adding onepassed
    Adding twofailed
    Adding threepassed
    • 





Rule: Outside of a testthat run, run() reports the run with CucumberProgressReporter


As there is no testthat reporter to show it. Pass reporter = NULL to report nothing.


Scenario: run() outside of a testthat run shows which step failed
  • Given a file named "features/calculate.feature" with

    Feature: Calculate
  Scenario: Adding one
    Then one plus 1 is 3
    • 

  • And a file named "features/steps.R" with
    then("one plus {int} is {int}", function(n, sum, context) {
  expect_equal(1 + n, sum)
})
    • 

  • When I run outside of a testthat run and it fails
    source("features/steps.R")
run("features")
    • 

  • Then the output includes these lines in order:
    Scenario: Adding one
x Then one plus 1 is 3
Step "one plus 1 is 3" failed
    • 





Scenario: run() in a parallel testthat run is an error
  • When I run
    withr::with_envvar(
  c(TESTTHAT_IS_PARALLEL = "true"),
  testthat::test_local(reporter = "silent", stop_on_failure = FALSE)
)
    • 

  • Then the errors are
    [error]
Error: `run()` isn't supported in a parallel testthat run.
i Set `Config/testthat/parallel: false` in DESCRIPTION, or run the feature files with `cucumber::test()`.
    •
